executiveSummary.title: WHAT THE DATA SAYS
executiveSummary.narrative:
Renaissance New York Times Square Hotel appeared in at least one AI answer for 40% of the traveler needs we tested, and across every individual AI answer it appeared 25.4% of the time. Together, these results show how broadly AI recognizes the hotel and how consistently a traveler would encounter it.

Leisure Travel is Renaissance New York Times Square Hotel's clearest competitive strength. The hotel appeared in 31.8% of AI answers for these searches, compared with 6.4% for the comparable hotels used in this analysis — about 5 times as often as the comparable hotels used in this analysis. Among AI answers where hotel ranking could be measured, Renaissance New York Times Square Hotel appeared in the Top 3 61.1% of the time, showing how prominently it is positioned when AI includes it.

AI currently reflects 41.2% of the monitored facts and attributes that define the hotel, so important parts of the property proposition are not consistently represented in AI results. No comparable prior official monitoring period is available yet, so change over time is not shown.

sections.headline: Renaissance New York Times Square Hotel's most important issue is concentrated competitive displacement by New York Marriott Marquis, not a vague visibility problem.
sections.keyInsight: New York Marriott Marquis appears in 27 monitored scenarios where Renaissance New York Times Square Hotel is absent. That concentration matters more than a long competitor list because it identifies a repeatable substitution pattern. Related Reality Gap pressure includes Urban Lifestyle Hotel at 6.1% recognition, which may help explain why the hotel is not carried into those answers.
sections.whyItMatters: Leadership needs to understand why specific alternatives are surfaced instead of Renaissance New York Times Square Hotel in recurring demand contexts. Otherwise attention may stay on average scores while missing the concentrated leak. A displacement pattern that repeats is more actionable than a soft overall visibility narrative.
sections.focusNow: Focus first on the demand contexts where New York Marriott Marquis is consistently surfaced instead of Renaissance New York Times Square Hotel. Determine whether the relevant attributes and use cases are clearly represented across priority sources, and whether the hotel's own proposition is complete for those same contexts.
sections.whatToReview: Open the underlying displacement evidence for New York Marriott Marquis and compare attributes cited in those answers with Renaissance New York Times Square Hotel's first-party and major travel-source representation. Confirm whether the same cues appear when the hotel is present.
